chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Nadr, from Al-Qasim ibn Sulayman, from Abu Maryam Al-Ansari, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'A Mus'haf (parchment/copy of the Quran) fell into the sea, so they found it, and whatever was in it had been obliterated except for this Verse.'
Indeed, to Allah do all affairs eventually come.

key_terms.مُصْحَفٌ: A copy or parchment of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What happened to the Quranic parchment that fell into the sea?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on miscellaneous miracles, this narration by Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the divine protection of the Quranic text through a specific, isolated preservation event. The survival of 'Indeed, to Allah do all affairs eventually come' (42:53) amidst the erasure of other verses underscores the concept of *I'jaz* (inimitability) and serves as a tangible sign of God’s authority over all matters, a theme resonant with Shia theological emphasis on divine decree and the enduring nature of revelation.
